title: Repulse
summary: REPULSE, noun repuls'. [Latin repulsa, from repello; re and pello, to drive.] 1. A being checked in advancing, or driven back by force. The enemy met with a repulse and retreated. 2. Refusal; denial.

inlines.v: REPULSE, noun repuls'. [Latin repulsa, from repello; re and pello, to drive.] 1. A being checked in advancing, or driven back by force. The enemy met with a repulse and retreated. 2. Refusal; denial. REPULSE, verb transitive repuls'. [Latin repulsus, repello.] To repel; to beat or drive back as, to repulse an assailant or advancing enemy.
